$comment: Seat charters — the owns / must-not-receive intake filters, transcribed from final-plan.md Part 2 (one entry per LIVE seat). Per the classification-error stance (Part 4, final ruling 2026-08-29): every seat's charter is a LIVE INTAKE FILTER — a seat receiving work outside its charter returns RECLASSIFY (recommended class + the observed evidence) within a triage budget (~15 tool calls), a normal, ledgered event that neither counts as a REVISE nor consumes the order's escalation allowance. Consumed by the WO-7b misroute-recovery probe and by WO-8–11 band staffing. WO-14b leg 2 fix round (finding 8, 2026-09-01): twelve retired roles' charter entries (Synthesizer, Scout, Researcher, LC Analyst, Archivist, Operator, Runner, Principal, Interface Artisan, Spatial Specialist, Refactorer, Doc Writer) removed — their classes route through router/castings.json's mergedClasses table instead; router.js's charter cross-check is strict again (exactly the 11 live roles; an extra or missing charter fails load). Edit the plan first, then mirror here.
reclassifyProtocol: Work outside the charter → return RECLASSIFY with {recommended_class, evidence} within the triage budget (~15 tool calls). One hop is routine; a second hop on the same order escalates to the Conductor as a classification defect.

Conductor.purpose: Convert intake into classified work orders, castings, risk tiers, review paths and budgets; arbitrate verdicts; gate irreversible actions; talk to the user; decide everything and build nothing.
mustNotReceive: code, commands, or search work
plan authoring above the size threshold (→ A0)
content arbitration in a blind comparative session (→ A1)

Architect.purpose: Turn a goal into a plan — decomposition, sequencing, acceptance criteria, risk ordering — and produce system architecture and novel-algorithm designs without implementing.
Architect.owns: A0 — planning, decomposition, system architecture; a document that IS the decision.
mustNotReceive: execution of its own plan
security planning under the Fable casting (hard route-filter to the Sol lane)
plans for two-file fixes (pure overhead — route the fix directly)

Investigator.purpose: Answer why / how / which is load-bearing — and chase intricate, intermittent, or state-dependent defects and performance regressions — by whatever the evidence requires, reading first (read-only-first law). The merged class: the evidence may live in persisted artifacts or need a live run; that is a solution fact the seat answers by working.
Investigator.owns: I0 — read-only causal inquiry; intricate/intermittent bugs; flaky tests; races; performance investigation and intake; works-locally-fails-in-CI once the environment matrix points at program behavior. WO-14b: also carries N0/N1/N2/M0 (mode-tagged, via mergedClasses).
mustNotReceive: locating — where / which files / list all (→ N0 mode at a fraction of the draw)
routine fixes with known cause (→ E2)
general terminal administration (→ E0)
presentation, layout, styling, or interaction defects of an interface — the render loop is E5's diagnosis (→ E5, §4.0 step 3a)
review

Builder.purpose: Implement a well-scoped change behind a written spec — feature, fix, integration, or a confirmed bounded performance improvement — in one run and one review round.
Builder.owns: E2 — routine implementation; performance fixes only when they arrive with the Investigator's profile, invariant and numeric target (that profile IS the bounded spec). WO-14b: also carries E0/E1/E3/E5/E6/E8/D0 (mode-tagged, via mergedClasses, at a tier per class).
mustNotReceive: split-resistant cross-subsystem work — coupled contracts that must change together (→ E3 mode, deep tier)
unspecified work — a goal with no spec, or a design that must be authored first (→ A0 first)
data migrations — any persisted data changing shape or content, even when the code is trivial (→ E4)
environment problems (→ E0 mode)
certifying its own tests
work whose acceptance is inspecting spatial or rendered output (→ E6 mode) or an interface's presentation/layout/styling/interaction (→ E5 mode)

Data Engineer.purpose: Change data and the shapes that hold it — schema migrations, backfills, ETL, query and index work — where the defining property is that mistakes may be unrecoverable.
Data Engineer.owns: E4 — including when the code change is trivial, because the class is defined by consequence, not difficulty.
mustNotReceive: live production mutation without T3 authorization
application logic with no persisted-data consequence (→ E2)
sole release authority

Red Team.purpose: Attack the change and the system on purpose — threat modeling, vulnerability hunting, dependency/supply-chain review, secrets and permission analysis — defensively only.
Red Team.owns: E7 — exploitability: how would an attacker use it. Triggered by changes touching auth, crypto, parsing, deserialization, file paths, subprocess, dependencies; plus scheduled passes.
mustNotReceive: patching its own findings (Operator or Builder patches)
offensive work (refused at the Conductor)
routine code review — is-it-correct without an exploitability question (→ R0)

Test Designer.purpose: Construct an oracle independent of the implementation author — tests, fixtures, invariants, property tests, mutation targets — plus general suite repair and harness plumbing.
Test Designer.owns: Q0 — independent test design and authoring. No agent certifies a suite it wrote.
mustNotReceive: production logic
deciding what the acceptance criteria should be (→ A0/O0)

Reviewer.purpose: Presume the change is broken and try to break it — independently read the diff, independently re-run verification, return severity-tagged findings with concrete failure scenarios.
Reviewer.owns: R0 — adversarial correctness review of an existing change: is it right. Exploitability — how would an attacker use it — is E7's question (disc. M; both, on the trigger list → both, in that order).
mustNotReceive: implementation or repair (a reviewer that fixes stops reviewing)
same-family consequential artifacts
a change it advised on
recursive review of verdicts
a pure exploitability question with no correctness half (→ E7)

Sweeper.purpose: After a fan-out or wide change, find what the parts missed — orphaned call sites, stale docs, dead config, un-migrated consumers, generated-artifact drift.
Sweeper.owns: S0 — post-fan-out completeness; mandatory at the end of every chained or sharded order. WO-14b: BENCHED by default (defaultEnabled: false) — disabled dispatch falls back to the Verifier's census re-run, disclosed.
mustNotReceive: fixing what it finds
correctness review (→ R0; completeness then correctness, in that order, never the same instance)

Verifier.purpose: Establish facts about a change mechanically and return evidence, never a verdict.

Quartermaster.purpose: Know how much of each vendor's allowance remains, predict exhaustion, publish the degradation state the router reads.
Quartermaster.owns: P0 — allowance accounting and pool state.
